text_a: Visa Smart Debit/Smart Credit (VSDC) is a chip-based Visa card product supporting offline and online transactions, including Plus ATM transactions. VSDC cards work in conjunction with special chip-read terminals to approve or to decline transactions. VSDC offline transactions occur only between the cardholder's chip card and the terminal and do not go through VisaNet. VisaNet processes transactions online when processing triggers predetermined offline risk management procedures, or because of random selection parameters established by the issuer. For purchase transactions, the issuer may determine whether a cardholder signature or a PIN is required for cardholder verification. ATM transactions require a PIN. VSDC cards rely on cryptograms to ensure their security and the integrity of their offline and online transactions. Issuers selecting the Full Data implementation option verify the cryptogram submitted by Full Data acquirers in the 0100 authorization request. The card terminal authenticates the issuer's cryptogram in the 0110 authorization response to ensure the issuer that created the card is the issuer that approved the transaction. If V.I.P. performs processing for the Card Authentication feature on behalf of the issuer, V.I.P. validates the Authorization Request Cryptogram (ARQC) and provides the Authorization Response Cryptogram (ARPC) in the response. If the issuer participates in the Issuer Authentication feature, the issuer or V.I.P. generates a cryptogram (Authorization Response Cryptogram) sent to the card in the response so the card can validate the authorization response came from the correct issuer. Issuer participation is optional in the VSDC Card Authentication feature and in the Issuer Authentication feature.

changes.text: Account Funding Transaction – This transaction is used to fund accounts such as brokerage accounts and online stored value cards, from a Visa debit or credit card. Original Credit Transaction – This transaction enables funds to be credited to Visa account numbers for a purpose other than refunding a Visa purchase. Deferred Clearing Purchase Transaction – This transaction is used by such merchants as hotels and car rental agencies when the full purchase amount is not known at the time of transaction authorization. This transaction, used only by Visa POS acquirers, involves an authorization request followed by a deferred clearing advice message. Merchandise Return – A merchandise return transaction enables merchants to credit the account of a Visa POS cardholder who returns merchandise. Balance Inquiry – Balance inquiry transactions enable cardholders to check their balances at stand-alone merchant terminals and at the point of sale. If the issuer system cannot be reached, V.I.P. stand-in processing responds that issuer is not available. If the issuer is available and supports balance inquiries, VisaNet returns the account balance to the acquirer for display or for printing in the currency of the merchant or of the ATM. Issuers can optionally provide balance information in Visa POS purchase transaction responses. However, for an 0200 POS eFunds transactions (network 0029), the acquirer receives balance information in Field 54 – Additional Amounts regardless of the issuer's selected response options. (This processing does not apply to stand-alone balance inquiries.) ATM acquirers in the U.S. region must support balance inquiries; support of this transaction is optional for all other participants. PINs are required for full service 0200 POS balance inquiries. PINs may not be required if a chip card is being used in a full service 0100 POS balance inquiries. Address Verification Only (Visa POS) – This transaction is used by merchants like direct marketing firms and airlines to verify a cardholder's address before submitting a purchase transaction. Incremental Authorizations – Merchants use incremental authorization transactions when final purchase amounts are unknown. Incremental authorizations enable merchants to obtain approval on additional amount, after the merchant uses an estimated amount to initiate and authorize the original transaction. Merchants can only do an incremental authorization in conjunction with an estimated authorization. When merchants determine final amounts, they submit supplemental, incremental authorization, or authorization reversal for cancelled purchases. Endpoints must not decline incremental authorizations by treating them as duplicate. In incremental authorization requests and their reversals, field 11 and field 37 values matches corresponding values in original authorization requests and the Transaction identifier (TID) value matches corresponding values in original authorization responses. Acquirers perform clearing using a single clearing transaction for the final amount, the issuer can match the incremental authorizations to the original estimated amount. Participating CPS POS Acquirers must include the TID from the initial authorization in any subsequent incremental authorization request or reversal.

(This processing does not apply to stand-alone balance inquiries.) ATM acquirers in the U.S. region must support balance inquiries; support of this transaction is optional for all other participants. Incremental Authorizations – Certain merchants, such as hotels, car rental companies, and airlines, initiate incremental authorization transactions when the final amount of the purchase is unknown. The incremental authorization contains an estimated amount that may vary significantly from the final transaction amount. When the merchant determines the final amount, it submits a supplemental, or incremental, authorization or a single authorization reversal if the purchase is cancelled. Endpoints must not decline incremental authorizations by treating them as duplicate transactions. In incremental authorization requests and their reversals, the field 11 and field 37 values match the corresponding values in the original authorization request message, and the field 62.2 value matches the corresponding value in the original authorization response message.
